Directorate Of Home ... on 12 April, 2024
IN THE COURT OF SH. AJAY GOEL: PRESIDING OFFICER  INDUSTRIAL TRIBUNAL-I, ROUSE AVENUE DISTRICT  COURTS, NEW DELHI. 
 F.24 (05)/ID/WD/10/CO-I/LAB/2024/05  Dated 05.02.2024 POIT No: 21/2024 Workmen Shri Rajender Kumar & Ors.(As per Annexure-A) working with the Directorate of Home Guards through the General Secretary Delhi Parshasan Vikas Vibhag Industrial Employees Union,
Aggarwal Bhawan, Tis Hazari, G.T. Road, Delhi-110054.
 Vs.
The Management of Directorate of Home Guards through its Director General,
Nishkam Seva Bhawan, CTI Complex, Raja Garden, New Delhi- 110027.
 Date of Institution : 06.02.2024  Date of Arguments : 12.04.2024  Date of Award : 12.04.2024  AWAR D 1. The Labour Department, Govt. of the National Capital Territory of Delhi has referred this dispute arising between the parties named above for adjudication to this Tribunal vide notification F.24/(05)/ID/WD/10/CO-I/LAB/2024/05 dated 05.02.2024 with following terms of the reference:-
POIT No. 21/2024 Page 1 of 31  "Whether the claimants (as per Annexure-A) are  covered under the definition of "workman" as  defined u/s 2(s) of I.D. Act, 1947? And if so  whether are entitled to remain in service with the  management till 60 years of their age? And if yes  to what relief are they entitled to and what  directions are necessary in this respect?" 
2. Statement of claim was filed on behalf of the 1433 workmen through Delhi Prashashan Vikas Vibhag Industrial Employees Union, whose particulars are given in the Annexure-A to this award. 
It is submitted therein that the workmen were employed by the management from 2009 to 2012. The management advertised the Rajender Kumar And 1432 Ors vs The Management Of Directorate Of Home ... on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96818398/
1 vacancies, attracting numerous applicants. A written test as well as physical test was conducted, and the candidates meeting the merit criteria successfully were then appointed. Thereafter, they were given training by the management. It is further submitted that Management serves as a manpower contractor to various government agencies/user departments for the work of Drivers,
Peons, Data Entry Operators, Multi Tasking Staff etc. These workmen are stated to adhere to eight-hour shifts, sometimes extending beyond or covering double shifts in a day. Initially the workers were stated to be paid minimum wages, but from 2018,
workmen are paid salaries equivalent to the lowest government employees, without entitlement to pension, gratuity, provident fund,
or any other social security benefits. They are also not entitled to weekly or any paid holidays, and earn their full wages only if they work the entire month without breaks. Any absence leads to a proportional deduction in their salary. It is stated that despite the POIT No. 21/2024 Page 2 of 31  extra hours or shifts, they do not receive overtime pay but are paid at the regular rate for additional shifts. The respondent management operates at its full capacity with a sanctioned strength of 10285 employees, and deploy its workers to various user department/agencies such as transport department, traffic, railways etc, wherein they perform the work of Drivers, Peons, Data Entry Operators, Multi-Tasking Staff etc. Despite initial engagement for three-years, the management extended their tenure from time to time, with all of them working for at least 12 to 15 years, underlining the perennial nature of their jobs. 
3. It is also submitted that the management is not a "voluntary organization" but an industry under Section 2(j) of the Industrial Disputes Act, engaging in recruitment, training, and deployment of workers to various agencies, thus meeting the criteria set in the Bangalore Water Supply & Sewerage Board v. A. Rajappa, (1978) 2 SCC 213. The workers performing skilled/unskilled/clerical nature of duties which falls under the definition of workman in Section 2(s) of the Act. Initially, they were engaged for three years, their tenure has been extended multiple times, indicating the ongoing and perennial nature of their work. It is averred that despite this, the management has sought to circumvent their obligations by claiming engagement of the workers under the Bombay Home Guards Act, 1947, misrepresenting the real nature of employment relationship and exploiting the workmen. It is also stated that the Management vide notification dated 15.02.2019 amended Rule 3 and 9 of the Delhi Home Guards Rules 1959 and replaced the word "fifty years" to "sixty years",
hence, a homeguard can continue to be a member till he attains the age of sixty years. But, by limiting the tenure of office, the Management is arbitrarily denying employment to Workmen who are below the age of sixty years. It is also submitted that the management has indulged in unfair labour practices by treating the workers as "homeguards volunteers" and extracting the permanent and perennial nature of work with the object of depriving the benefits arising out of their permanent status. The workmen have prayed that an award be made in their favour declaring the claimants as "workman" who are entitled to all the benefits of its workmen and they be also held entitled to be deployed till the age of 60 years irrespective of the terms of office.

2 4. Written Statement filed on behalf of the management narrating the history of the evolution of the concept of Homeguards. During World War-II, the United Kingdom established the Home Guards as a voluntary local defense organization. Following this, India introduced Home Guards in Bombay on 6th December 1946 to aid police in managing civil unrest and communal riots. Consequently,
various Indian states created similar voluntary forces for public safety and emergency response. 
Lateron, in response to the 1962 Chinese Aggression, the Centre recommended consolidating these groups into a unified, volunteer-based national force called the "Home Guards". The Directorate General of Home Guards, established in 1959 under the Bombay Home Guards Act of 1947 and the Delhi Home Guards Rules of 1959, operates as a voluntary organization dedicated to protecting people, property, and public safety. Broadly, they were assigned with the following duties such as serving as police auxiliaries for internal security, assisting in emergencies like air raids, fires, floods,
and epidemics, organizing units for essential services (e.g., transportation, engineering, fire- fighting, medical aid, and utility operation), promoting communal harmony and protecting vulnerable societal groups, and engaging in socio-economic and welfare activities, including education, health, and development programs. As far as their terms of office is concerned, according to the Delhi Home Guards Rules, the term of office of a member is initially for three years,
extendable by two additional years vide notification dated 05.06.2008 based on discipline, service record, conduct, and physical fitness. Furthermore, their terms extended again in special circumstances through notifications within a month of discharge. 
5. The management has further submitted that the Hon'ble Supreme Court has consistently held that the Home Guards is a disciplined volunteer workforce and it cannot be considered equivalent to workmen or civil servants. Therefore, this tribunal does not have jurisdiction to entertain the present dispute and it deserves dismissal on this ground alone. Apart from this the management has relied upon the case of Rajesh Mishra vs. Govt. of NCT of Delhi (2002) SCC OnLine Del 483 wherein it was held that Homeguards is a Disciplined Volunteer Force and there is no master servant relationship between the government and the Homeguards. Likewise, reliance is also placed upon the cases of Man Sukh Lal Rawat & Ors. vs. UOI & Ors., 1999 IV AD (Delhi) 469, Grah Rakshak,
Home Guards Welfare Association vs. State of H.P. & Ors., denied the relief of regularization or regular appointment to the Homeguards and they are used during the emergency purposes as outlined in the HomeGuards Act. Based on these judgments, it is submitted by the management that Delhi Home Guards is a voluntary organization established under specific acts and operates as per the Delhi Home Guards Rules, 1959. The petitioners/claimants have wrongly categorized themselves as workmen instead of Home Guard Volunteer rendering their services voluntarily in accordance with the Act and Rules, therefore, they are not entitled for continuity till age of superannuation as claimed by them. Lastly, it is submitted that the present claim is without any cause of action, arising out of misreading of relevant legal provisions, imaginary cause of action. It is prayed on behalf of the management that the instant claim is liable to be dismissed as, it does not establish either factually or legally any case warranting the exercise of the jurisdiction by Industrial Tribunal cum Labour Courts. 
6. An application under Order X Rule 2 of Civil Procedure Code, 1908 was filed on behalf of the workmen for calling the concerned officer who has the authority for taking decision on the relief/reference sought, which was allowed. The Commandant HQs was consequently examined by Rajender Kumar And 1432 Ors vs The Management Of Directorate Of Home ... on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96818398/
3 this Tribunal u/o X Rule 2 C.P.C and his statement to that effect was recorded.
7. No rejoinder is filed on behalf of the workman. After the completion of proceedings, the following issues were framed based on the pleadings of the parties:
(i) As per terms of reference (ii) Relief 8. To prove its case, the workmen examined, Sh.Vijay Kumar S/o Sh. Murari Lal on behalf of all the workers and filed his Affidavit Ex. WW1/A in lieu of examination-in-chief. He relied upon documents Ex. WW1/1 to Ex. WW1/10 - copy of advertisement dated 23.01.2024 issued by the management, copy of notice dated 11.01.2024 issued by the management, copy of resolution dated 02.01.2024 of the executive committee of the union, copies of appointment letters of some of the workers (colly), copies of transfer orders, experience letters issued by the management, copies of extension orders/notifications, copy of notification dated 15.02.2019, copy of statement of claim filed before the conciliation officer, copy of application for maintaining status quo in the service conditions of the workers and copy of reply filed by the management. The Workmen witness (WW-1) after tendering his evidence was consequently cross-examination by the AR for the management. Pursuant to which, the workmen's evidence was closed. 
9. Per contra, the management examined Sh. Dhrmendra Singh Rawat S/o Late Sh. N.S. Rawat,
working as Commandant Directorate General of Home Guards. He was examined-in-chief and subsequently cross-examined by the AR for the workman. Subsequently, the management evidence was closed. The management also filed a reply to the Affidavit, even though there is no provision for the same, yet the reply is taken on record. Thereafter, the case was fixed for final arguments. 
10. Final arguments have been heard at length as advanced by both the parties. This tribunal has gone through the documents, pleadings as well as arguments of both the parties. This tribunal has also gone through the reply of the affidavit of workmen as well as written synopsis cum note of arguments and the same are dealt with by this Tribunal in following paras. 
11. My issue was wise findings are as follows: 
Issue No. 1: As per terms of reference "Whether the claimants (as per Annexure-A)
are covered under the definition of "workman" as defined u/s 2(s) of I.D. Act, 1947?
And if so whether are entitled to remain in service with the management till 60 years of their age? And if yes to what relief are they entitled to and what directions are necessary in this respect?" 
12. Before moving on to the merits of this case, even though no objection pertaining to the espousal is taken by the management yet this tribunal has to see if the same is properly espoused by the union.

4 13. In order to prove the proper espousal, the Ld. A.R. for the workmen has placed reliance upon Ex.
WW1/3 i.e. resolution dated 02.01.2024 passed by the Delhi Prashashan Vikas Vibhag Industrial Employees' Union for raising an industrial dispute in favour of the workmen wherein it is unanimously resolved to raise an industrial dispute in faviour of Sh. Rajender Kumar & Ors.
working with Directorate of Homeguards and members of Delhi Prashashan Vikas Vibhag Industrial Employees' Union for declaring them as employees/workmen of Directorate of Homeguards and allow them to continue in service till they attain the age of 60 years irrespective of terms of their office and to maintain status quo in their service conditions till the pendency of the industrial dispute. He also placed reliance upon the judgement of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Omji Srivastava and Ors. vs. P.W.D./C.P.W.D., 2023/DHC/002013 decided on 17.03.2023, wherein the Hon'ble Delhi High Court after relying upon the case of Hon'ble Supreme Court in J.H. Jadhav v.
M/s Forbes Gokak Ltd., Civil Appeal No. 1089 of 2005, decided on 11.02.2005 has observed that there is no strict format required for a union espousing the cause of the workman, and this can vary and may also include resolutions or other forms of evidence depending on the case to case. Even in the absence of formal resolution, the court relied upon various documents such as statement of claim filed before the conciliation officer, legal demand notice, authorisation letters etc. among other documents and held that the cause of the workman have been properly espoused by the union.
14. Likewise, the issue of espousal if any has to be taken at the first instance i.e. when the case is pending before the conciliation officer, and it should not be an afterthought plea. Reliance in this regard is placed upon the Division Bench judgement of Hon'ble Kerala High Court in Mangalam Publications (India) Pvt. Ltd. v. Saju George, W.A. No. 964 of 2020, decided on 01.12.2020, wherein the management failed to take the plea of espousal at the initial stage, and subsequently, when the dispute was taken up for consideration by the Tribunal after being referred by the union, it is not permissible for the management to argue that the cause of the workman was not supported by the union. Moreover, the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the case of Pratap Singh & Anr. vs. Municipal Corporation of Delhi, WP(C) No. 676/2013 vide order dated 04.02.2013 reversed the findings of the Ld. Labour Court on the issue of espousal by categorising it as hypertechnical and held that the cause of the workman is properly espoused by the union. 
15. Even otherwise, in the present case, the statement of claim (Ex. WW1/8) filed before the conciliation officer by the Delhi Prashashan Vikas Vibhag Industrial Employees' Union. The resolution dated 02.01.2024 i.e. Ex. WW1/3, wherein the union decided to raise an industrial dispute in favour of the workmen have also been placed on record. Also, this case pertains to a total of 1433 workers who are contesting this dispute, this fact itself on the prima facie suggests that their case is supported by a massive majority of their workers. Moreover, no objections pertaining to the espousal were taken by the management, even the workmen witness (WW-1) was not cross-examined by the AR for the management on these aspects. Therefore, this tribunal has no reasons to cast doubt on the espousal placed on record by the Delhi Prashashan Vikas Vibhag Industrial Employees' Union. The management witness (MW-1) has also admitted the authenticity of the documents placed on record by the workman. In view of this discussion above, the workmen have placed sufficient material on record, hence, the tribunal is of the opinion that the cause of the workman has been properly espoused by the Delhi Prashashan Vikas Vibhag Industrial Employees'
Union.

5 16. Now the issue before this tribunal is whether the claimants concerned fall within the definition of workman u/s 2(s) of the I.D. Act and are the employees of the management or they are volunteers as claimed by the management. 
17. On merits, the AR for the workman has argued that the workers in the present case have never worked as "voluntary homeguards" as stated by the management. In fact, they have been performing the permanent and perennial nature of duties such as Driver, Multi Tasking Staff, Data Entry Operator etc. since their initial dates of joining. It is argued that the concerned workmen were never given any call-out/emergency duties as outlined in the Bombay Home Guards Act, as well as Rules. 
To the contrary, they were made to perform perennial work continuously and uninterruptedly for as long as 15 years. The management has indulged in an unfair labour practice as enumerated in Item No. 10 of Fifth Schedule r/w Section 2(ra) of the I.D. Act by extracting the work of Driver, MTS,
DEO etc. for as long as 15 years under the garb of "Home Guards Volunteers" solely with the object to deprive them with the status and benefits of a permanent employee. Further, the workmen are entitled to be in service till they attain the age of 60 years, but they are kept on fixed tenure and the Management is trying to terminate their services by issuing fresh advertisement. He further argued that the permanent employees of the Management are superannuated at the age of 60 years. It is also argued that the workmen have been performing work and duties similar to regular DEO, driver,
MTS of the Management, therefore they should be given pay, allowances and service conditions at par with the similar posts. 
18 . On the other hand, the AR for the management has placed reliance upon several judgements of Hon'ble Supreme Court as well as Hon'ble High Court i.e. Rajesh Mishra vs. Govt. of NCT of Delhi (2002) SCC OnLine Del 483, Man Sukh Lal Rawat & Ors. vs. UOI & Ors., 1999 IV AD (Delhi) 469,
Grah Rakshak, Home Guards Welfare Association vs. State of H.P. & Ors., wherein the Hon'ble Courts have time and again reiterated that the Homeguards is a voluntary organization and denied the relief of regularization or regular appointment to the Homeguards and they are used during the emergency purposes as outlined in the HomeGuards Act. Based on these judgments, it is submitted by the management that Delhi Home Guards is a voluntary organization established under specific acts and operates as per the Delhi Home Guards Rules, 1959. The Hon'ble Supreme Court has consistently held that the Home Guards is a disciplined volunteer workforce and it cannot be considered equivalent to workmen or civil servants. Therefore, this tribunal does not have jurisdiction to entertain the present dispute and it deserves dismissal on this ground alone. 
19. The definition of workman has been defined in Section 2(s) of the I.D. Act, which states as follows:
"(s) 'workman' means any person (including an apprentice) employed in any industry to do any manual, unskilled, skilled technical, sales promotion, operational, clerical or supervisory work or any work for the promotion of sales for hire or reward,
whether the terms of employment be expressed or implied, and for the purposes of any proceeding under this Act in relation to an industrial dispute, includes any such person who has been dismissed, discharged or retrenched in connection with, or as a consequence of, that dispute, or whose dismissal, discharge or retrenchment has led Rajender Kumar And 1432 Ors vs The Management Of Directorate Of Home ... on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96818398/
6 to that dispute, but does not include any such person-- (i) who is subject to the Air Force Act, 1950 (45 of 1950), or the Army Act, 1950 (46 of 1950), or the Navy Act, 1957 (62 of 1957); or (ii) who is employed in the police service or as an officer or other employee of a prison; or (iii) who is employed mainly in a managerial or administrative capacity; or (iv) who, being employed in a supervisory capacity, draws wages exceeding one thousand six hundred rupees per mensem or exercises, either by the nature of the duties attached to the office or by reason of the powers vested in him, functions mainly of a managerial nature." [Vide A.P. Act 22 of 2008, S. 2 (w.e.f. the date to be notified)]
20. As per the definition of the workman, a person who has been employed in any industry performing the manual, unskilled, technical, skilled, sales promotion, operation, clerical or supervisory work for hire and reward will fall under the definition of workman. The aforesaid definition has strictly barred certain categories of employees under the ambit of Industrial Disputes Act. Those establishments which are subject to the Air Force Act, Army Act, Navy Act, employees those were employed in the police service or an officer/employee in prison, or those who were employed in a managerial/administrative capacity. 
21. The explicit bar given under the exceptions as stipulated in the definition of workman nowhere bars Department of Homeguards/management herein. Secondly no objection pertaining to the management not being an industry has been raised, hence, the management being an "industry" is also not disputed. Even otherwise, the management fulfills the triple test of industry as laid by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Bangalore Water Supply & Sewerage Board v. A. Rajappa, (1978) 2 SCC 213 i.e. where there is a (i) systematic activity, (ii) organized by co-operation between employer and employee (the direct and substantial element is chimerical) (iii) for the production and/or distribution of goods and services calculated to satisfy human wants and wishes (not spiritual or religious but inclusive of material things or services geared to celestial bliss e.g. making, on a large scale prasad or food), prima facie, there is an 'industry' in that enterprise. Likewise, in the present case, the management witness admitted in his cross- examination that the management is having various departments such as vigilance department, accounts department, establishment department, training department etc. it is also admitted to be correct that the workman work in a systematic manner to fulfill the requisite requirements of society. Hence, in view of the admission of the management witness as well as no objection raised on behalf of the management pertaining to them being an "industry" under the Industrial dispute, this tribunal is of the opinion that the management indeed is industry under the I.D. Act.
22. Now, as far as the question of claimants being workman is concerned, it is a well settled position of law that the designation of the workers is not the criterion for determination of the status of an Rajender Kumar And 1432 Ors vs The Management Of Directorate Of Home ... on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96818398/
7 employee since the nature of duties are taken into consideration to ascertain whether an employee is a workman or not as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court and various High Courts.. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Hussan Mithu Mhasvadkar v. Bombay Iron & Steel Labour Board, (2001) 7 SCC 394 has observed that designation alone is not a decisive factor for determining the issue of workman, one has to examine the predominant nature of duties, power and functions of the worker. 
23. In the instant case, a total of 1433 workers have approached this tribunal stating that the management under the garb of "homeguards volunteers" have been utilizing their services for performing the work of Driver, MTS, DEO etc. The Written Statement filed on behalf of the management did not specifically answer the contentions made by the workers pertaining to the actual nature of duties discharged by them. Therefore, this tribunal while exercising its power under Order X Rule 2 recorded the statement of the concerned official, S.K. Shokeen (Commandant) of the management in order to arrive at the real nature of the dispute between the parties. Upon examination of the said officer, it emerged that the concerned claimants indeed were performing the duties of Drivers, Peons, Clerks, MTS, Data Entry Operators in the departments and the same are predominantly of unskilled and clerical nature. It is also stated that the management has recruited the concerned claimants and they worked under its control and supervision. They are paid wages/daily duty allowances on a monthly basis after receiving it from the user department wherein they are deployed to perform their services. The said claimants are stated to be working against the sanctioned posts/strength, and that there are a large number of posts/strengths which are still vacant in Delhi, as the total strength is 10285/- but only 8200 workers are working. The said claimants are stated to be working continuously and uninterruptedly without any break since the date of joining and engaged in a perennial nature of work. 
24. The examination of the management under Order X Rule 2 makes it clear that the claimants are performing unskilled and clerical duties, such as Drivers, Peons, Clerks, MTS, and Data Entry Operators. The management confirms that the claimants were recruited by them and are working under their control and supervision. The management describes their role in paying wages and allowances to the claimants, which are provided by the user department and paid to them on a monthly basis by the management alone. The witness submitted that the claimants are working against sanctioned posts, and there is a large number of vacancies, especially in Delhi, where there is a significant discrepancy between sanctioned strength (10285) and actual workers (8200). It is also admitted that the claimants have been working continuously without any break since their date of joining, engaged in work of a perennial nature. Meaning thereby, there remained no dispute about the actual nature of duties being performed by them, and the fact they have been discharging their duties, thus the controversy with respect to them performing the work of Driver, MTS, Data Entry Operator and that they have been working continuously and uninterruptedly without any break since the date of joining remained undisputed. 
25. Attention of this tribunal is drawn towards the advertisements for the year 2008 for recruitment for male/female Home Guard (Home Guards) volunteers in Delhi for 4650 posts/strength. 
Likewise, applications were also invited from professional (tradesman) Home Guard (Home Guards) for 550 posts/strength for both men and women for performing the work of Computer Operator, Professional Light/Heavy Vehicle Driver, Electrician, Auto Electrician, Auto Mechanic,
Rajender Kumar And 1432 Ors vs The Management Of Directorate Of Home ... on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96818398/
8 Draftsman, Carpenter, Stenographer, Welder, Fitter, Mason, Cook, Plumber and Pump Operator. 
An application fee of Rs. 25/- is also charged for enrollment in the "voluntary" service. Similar advertisements pertaining to the year 2011 are also placed on record. 
26. The claimants pursuant to such advertisements applied and underwent selection procedure conducted by the selection board of the management. The said selection procedure consisted of a written test as well as a physical test and only upon successfully clearing the selection procedure, the claimants were engaged by the management and given a training of 35 days. These facts are not disputed by the management. 
27. This tribunal has failed to understand when the very purpose of the Bombay Home Guards Act to create a group of volunteers whose service can be utilized for emergency call-out duties, then why the claimants after their training were deployed in various user departments in a routine manner for performing the permanent and perennial nature of duties of Driver, MTS, DEO etc. Section 2 and 4 of the Bombay Home Guards Act, 1947 outlines that the members of Homeguards are supposed to discharge functions and duties in relation to the protection of persons, the security of property and public safety, and when call-out/emergency duties are given they are empowered with the same powers/protection as an officer of police appointed under any Act for the time being in force. 
Herein, no evidence whatsoever in the oral or documentary has been led by the management to show that the claimants during the entire service period of 15 years were ever given call-out/emergency duties in accordance with the act and given power or protection at par with the police personnel. In fact, the management witness (MW-1) in his cross-examination failed to mention even a single instance where the claimants were workers on mission/emergency call-out duties. Instead, the claimant's after their selection by the management were given 35-days training and right after that they were deployed in various user departments under the name of "home guards volunteers" in the absence of any call-out/emergency duty whatsoever. 
28. The cross-examination of the management witness (MW-1) sheds light on several facts of the present matter. MW1 admitted about the uninterrupted employment of workmen from 2009-2012 to till date, detailing their recruitment and selection procedure which included public advertisements, written and physical tests prior to their hiring. He also admitted that these employees received rigorous training and were subsequently deployed in various user departments. 
He admitted the daily duty hours of the claimants and their additional responsibilities during national events. Furthermore, he admitted that the management exercises control over the claimants, including the granting or denying of leave. Notably, the management led no evidence to the effect that the claimants were being called out for duties only for missions or emergency. The relevant portion of the cross-examination of the management witness is as follows:
"The documents filed by the workmen/their union on the court record are not in dispute and the same are admitted by us (document shown). It is correct that the concerned workmen joined into the employment of the management from the year 2009 to 2012 and since then they are working continuously and uninterruptedly. Vol. 
In our organisation instead of using word 'Management' we use the word 'Head Quarters of Directorate General of Home Guards, Delhi'. It is correct that prior to Rajender Kumar And 1432 Ors vs The Management Of Directorate Of Home ... on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96818398/
9 appointment of the workmen, the post was advertised in the newspapers. The concerned workmen in this case and other applicant applied for the job. 
It is correct that these workmen were duly selected by the Selection Board of the Management. The concerned workmen were found suitable and selected by the Selection Board which was duly constituted by the management. Vol. We do not use the word 'workmen' in our organisation, but we use the word 'Home Guard Volunteers'. 
It is correct that the work and conduct of the concerned workmen is satisfactory. It is correct that prior to the appointment of the workmen a written test as well as physical test was held. It is correct that as per the merit, 1.5 time of the candidates were selected and then physical test was held and then the workmen who qualified were appointed. Vol. In our organisation we do not use the word 'appointment' but use the word 'Enrollment'. It is correct that after their selection, the concerned workmen were given 35 days rigorous training. It is correct that after that training,
the workmen were given appointment letters. 
It is correct that after the selection of the concerned workmen they were deployed in various departments of Govt. of NCT. It is also correct that over there, they are performing the duties of Driver, Peon, Data Entry Operator, MTS, Carpenter, etc.
Vol. The supposedly primary job as per the Compendium of Instructions is of maintenance of law and order. It is correct that the retirement/superannuation job is 60 years for regular employees working with the management including myself. It is correct that all the concerned workmen are working 8 hours duties per day. It is correct that the concerned workmen are performing their duties 365 days a year. It is correct that the concerned workmen performed double duties on occasion of Republic Day, Independence Day and events like G20, etc. Vol. The workmen perform voluntary nature of the work as per the Act of the management. It is correct that there are 10285 sanctioned posts/strength of Home Guard Volunteers. 
It is correct that the concerned workmen have been paid wages in the minimum of the payscale of MTS since 2016. Vol. We do not use the word 'Wages' but 'Duty Allowance'. It is correct that the respondent/management has full control and supervision over the workmen. It is correct that the appointment letters, wages,
supervision and control, transfer and issuance of memo, etc. is done by the management only. It is correct that the leave permission when sought by the concerned workmen is given by the officials of the management. It is correct that the workmen have not been given the benefit of provident fund, gratuity, pension and any other social security. 
It is correct that the management is having various department such as Vigilance Department, Accounts Department, Establishment Department, Training Department, etc. It is correct that the workmen work in a systematic manner to fulfill Rajender Kumar And 1432 Ors vs The Management Of Directorate Of Home ... on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96818398/
10 the requisite requirement of society. I cannot say if the concerned management is on the pattern of Group 4 (Manpower Supply). The document containing the various posts in the management and their payscales is exhibited as Ex. MW1/W-1. 
It is correct that the concerned workmen are also performing the similar duties and working hours as mentioned in Ex. MW1/W-1. Vol. As per Compendium of Instructions the job of the workmen is supposedly of law and order. 
It is correct that the concerned workmen can also perform their duties till they attain the age of 60 years like other workers working with the management. Vol. The regular workers with the management are not allowed to work elsewhere, whereas the concerned workmen, there is no such condition. The management has not filed any document to show that any of the concerned workmen is doing work elsewhere as well as with the management simultaneously. It is incorrect to suggest that the management has not filed any such document as none of them are working elsewhere. 
The management has not placed any document to show that the workmen have ever worked on mission/emergency call of duties since their initial appointment to till date. It is incorrect to suggest that no such document has been filed by the management as they have never worked on mission/emergency call of duties. I cannot mention the example here however the treatment as bonded labour by the management. It is incorrect to suggest that the management has indulged in unfair labour practices by not paying equal salary and same service conditions as has been given to the so called regular workers of the management.

Prior to their appointment, their posts were publicly advertised in newspapers, attracting applications from the workmen and others. The selection process was conducted by a duly constituted Selection Board of the Management, which found these workmen suitable and chose them based on their merits. Furthermore, the witness confirmed that after their selection, the workmen received 35 days of rigorous training before being formally issued appointment letters. Likewise, the management witness failed to show any document wherein the claimants were ever assigned any emergency/call-out duties during their entire service tenure of 15 long years.

30. The management has relied upon the judgments of Man sukh Lal (supra), where the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 1997 addressed the issue of home guards who were aggrieved by their discharge/termination from service. The court ruled against the right to reinstatement and regularization of home guards, holding that the Homeguards are fundamentally a volunteer organization, not an "employment" or "source of employment". The court highlighted that Homeguards are characterized by the voluntary offering of services for societal benefit, lacking stringent recruitment rules or prescribed duties. It was noted that Homeguards can come from various walks of life, including government and private sector employees, professionals, industrial workers, students, and others willing to dedicate their spare time for community service. The court maintained that regularizing volunteers or their activities would undermine the essential voluntary ethos and character of the Homeguards. Likewise, reliance is also placed upon Rajesh Mishra & Ors.

State of H.P. & Ors., Civil Appeal No. 2759 of 2015 (SLP (C) No. 12858 of 2009).
31. This tribunal has gone through the aforesaid judgements cited by the management and is of the considered opinion that the same are not applicable to the present case. In the present case, there is a difference between the service conditions of the claimants and that of petitioners in previous judgments, such as the Mansukh Lal(Supra) case. Earlier decisions were in the context of Homeguards Volunteers who were performing their duties in line with the mission and vision of the Bombay Home Guards Act. In the present case, the claimants, although categorized as "Homeguards", have been performing permanent and perennial duties across various departments at the behest of the management. Their responsibilities bear no relation to the emergency call-out duties outlined in the Act. Instead, they are required to work 8 hours a day, 7 days a week, and 365 days a year, often performing double duties on several occasions of national importance. 
32. As far as the question of "voluntariness" is concerned, once the claimants are enrolled as Homeguards, they are mandated to comply with every order assigned by their superior officers as stipulated in Rule 14 of the Delhi Home Guards Rules, 1959. Failure to comply subjects them to penalties for neglect or refusal to obey orders, as specified in Sections 6 and 7 of the Bombay Home Guards Act, 1947, as extended to the Union Territory of Delhi. Thus, the workers are compelled Rajender Kumar And 1432 Ors vs The Management Of Directorate Of Home ... on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96818398/
12 under all circumstances to perform various duties--whether as drivers, multi-tasking staff (MTS), or data entry operators (DEO) etc. The routine work and daily duty hours they are required to fulfill effectively preclude them from securing any other employment. Specifically, if an individual is tasked with driving duties for 8 hours a day, every day of the year, it is impossible for them to engage in any other gainful employment. 
33. The claimants have performed duties typically reserved for regular Class-IV and Class-III employees such as drivers, data entry operators, and multi-tasking staff for up to 15 years. Their 8-hour daily shifts, including weekends and holidays, sometimes even double shifts, render it impossible for them to hold other jobs. This continuous deployment contradicts the core purpose of the Homeguards, which is to provide emergency support, not regular employment. The management has not demonstrated that these workers were ever called for emergency duties as envisioned by the Bombay Home Guards Act over the past 15 years. Hence, the reliance of the management upon the Bombay Home Guards Act and Rules and the aforesaid judgements will not be of any help. Considering these prevailing circumstances, this Tribunal is constrained to lift the veil of "voluntary service" created by the management. Once the veil of "volunteer service" created by the management is pierced, then it emerges that there exists a relationship of master-servant or employer-employee between the management and the claimants.

Despite performing the regular nature of duties under the control and supervision of the management, they were not recognised as "workers" or "employees" but were treated merely as "volunteers". The management, under the guise of categorizing claimants "Homeguard volunteers", has denied them the status of "employees". They were required to work relentlessly i.e. 8 hours daily, without a single paid leave of Sundays, gazetted holidays, and festivals such as Holi and Diwali. On these occasions, they were often asked to perform double round the clock duties. It is also reiterated that while performing overtime-round the clock duties, they were not given wages in accordance with the overtime rates as prescribed under the law. When we consider the prevailing scenario, it is painful to note that the decision in Uma Devi (Supra) has not been properly understood and rather wrongly applied by Rajender Kumar And 1432 Ors vs The Management Of Directorate Of Home ... on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96818398/

Though this Court has emphasised that incumbents should be appointed on regular basis as per rules but new devise of making appointment on contract basis has been adopted, employment is offered on daily wage basis etc. in exploitative forms. This situation was not envisaged by Uma Devi (supra). The prime intendment of the decision was that the employment process should be by fair means and not by back door entry and in the available pay scale. 
That spirit of the Uma Devi (supra) has been ignored and conveniently over looked by various State Governments/ authorities. We regretfully make the observation that Uma Devi (supra) has not be implemented in its true spirit and has not been followed in its pith and substance. It is being used only as a tool for not regularizing the services of incumbents. They are being continued in service without payment of due salary for which they are entitled on the basis of Article 14, 16 read with Article 34 (1)

The employment cannot be on exploitative terms, whereas Uma Devi (supra) laid down that there should not be back door entry and every post should be filled by regular employment, but a new device has been adopted for making appointment on payment of paltry system on contract/adhoc basis or otherwise. He admitted "It is correct that the concerned workmen are also perfroming the similar duties and working hours as mentioned in Ex. MW1/W-1." Ex. MW1/W-1 is the schedule of posts existing in the management. 
The claimants are admittedly working under the direct control and supervision of management at various user departments. Admission is the best piece of evidence as per AIR 1960 SC 100 and Section 58 of Indian Evidence Act. However, it is also important to note that the workmen have not placed on record the designation of each worker and identified the nature of duties performed by each worker. annotations.text: 4. Written Statement filed on behalf of the management narrating the history of the evolution of the concept of Homeguards.
During World War-II, the United Kingdom established the Home Guards as a voluntary local defense organization.
Following this, India introduced Home Guards in Bombay on 6th December 1946 to aid police in managing civil unrest and communal riots.

Consequently,
various Indian states created similar voluntary forces for public safety and emergency response.
Lateron, in response to the 1962 Chinese Aggression, the Centre recommended consolidating these groups into a unified, volunteer-based national force called the "Home Guards".

The Directorate General of Home Guards, established in 1959 under the Bombay Home Guards Act of 1947 and the Delhi Home Guards Rules of 1959, operates as a voluntary organization dedicated to protecting people, property, and public safety.

Broadly, they were assigned with the following duties such as serving as police auxiliaries for internal security, assisting in emergencies like air raids, fires, floods,
and epidemics, organizing units for essential services (e.g., transportation, engineering, fire- fighting, medical aid, and utility operation), promoting communal harmony and protecting vulnerable societal groups, and engaging in socio-economic and welfare activities, including education, health, and development programs.

As far as their terms of office is concerned, according to the Delhi Home Guards Rules, the term of office of a member is initially for three years,
extendable by two additional years vide notification dated 05.06.2008 based on discipline, service record, conduct, and physical fitness.
Furthermore, their terms extended again in special circumstances through notifications within a month of discharge.

summary.ANALYSIS:
The aforesaid definition has strictly barred certain categories of employees under the ambit of Industrial Disputes Act.
21. The explicit bar given under the exceptions as stipulated in the definition of workman nowhere bars Department of Homeguards/management herein.
Even otherwise, the management fulfills the triple test of industry as laid by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Bangalore Water Supply & Sewerage Board v. A. Rajappa, (1978) 2 SCC 213 i.e. where there is a (i) systematic activity, (ii) organized by co-operation between employer and employee (the direct and substantial element is chimerical) (iii) for the production and/or distribution of goods and services calculated to satisfy human wants and wishes (not spiritual or religious but inclusive of material things or services geared to celestial bliss e.g. making, on a large scale prasad or food), prima facie, there is an 'industry' in that enterprise.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Hussan Mithu Mhasvadkar v. Bombay Iron & Steel Labour Board, (2001) 7 SCC 394 has observed that designation alone is not a decisive factor for determining the issue of workman, one has to examine the predominant nature of duties, power and functions of the worker.
The concerned workmen were found suitable and selected by the Selection Board which was duly constituted by the management.

It is correct that the work and conduct of the concerned workmen is satisfactory.
It is correct that prior to the appointment of the workmen a written test as well as physical test was held.

It is correct that after their selection, the concerned workmen were given 35 days rigorous training.
It is correct that after that training,

It is correct that after the selection of the concerned workmen they were deployed in various departments of Govt. of NCT.
The supposedly primary job as per the Compendium of Instructions is of maintenance of law and order.
The workmen perform voluntary nature of the work as per the Act of the management.
It is correct that the respondent/management has full control and supervision over the workmen.
It is correct that the appointment letters, wages,
supervision and control, transfer and issuance of memo, etc. is done by the management only.
It is correct that the leave permission when sought by the concerned workmen is given by the officials of the management.
It is correct that the workmen have not been given the benefit of provident fund, gratuity, pension and any other social security.

It is correct that the concerned workmen can also perform their duties till they attain the age of 60 years like other workers working with the management.
The management has not filed any document to show that any of the concerned workmen is doing work elsewhere as well as with the management simultaneously.
It is incorrect to suggest that the management has not filed any such document as none of them are working elsewhere.

The management has not placed any document to show that the workmen have ever worked on mission/emergency call of duties since their initial appointment to till date.
The concerned workmen are disciplined citizen.
It is correct that the nature of job which they are performing is of perennial nature which is likely to continue in the foreseen future.

Their responsibilities bear no relation to the emergency call-out duties outlined in the Act.
Failure to comply subjects them to penalties for neglect or refusal to obey orders, as specified in Sections 6 and 7 of the Bombay Home Guards Act, 1947, as extended to the Union Territory of Delhi.
The routine work and daily duty hours they are required to fulfill effectively preclude them from securing any other employment.
Specifically, if an individual is tasked with driving duties for 8 hours a day, every day of the year, it is impossible for them to engage in any other gainful employment.
33. The claimants have performed duties typically reserved for regular Class-IV and Class-III employees such as drivers, data entry operators, and multi-tasking staff for up to 15 years.
Their 8-hour daily shifts, including weekends and holidays, sometimes even double shifts, render it impossible for them to hold other jobs.
This continuous deployment contradicts the core purpose of the Homeguards, which is to provide emergency support, not regular employment.
The management has not demonstrated that these workers were ever called for emergency duties as envisioned by the Bombay Home Guards Act over the past 15 years.
Hence, the reliance of the management upon the Bombay Home Guards Act and Rules and the aforesaid judgements will not be of any help.
